passage: Abstract: 'only if the relationship between numerator and denominator is a straight line through the origin will the ratio be meaningful. If not, the ratio will misrepresent the true relationship between numerator and denominator.' Correction named in the abstract: regression techniques 'including analysis of covariance'. (Europe PMC record of PMID 24022766; abstract only, full text not open.)
faulty: Heart weight divided by body mass for each animal; one-sided two-sample (Welch) t test of that quotient between treated and untreated animals, claim holds when p < 0.05 with the treated mean larger. Documented parameter: the numerator-denominator relation is a straight line NOT through the origin (positive intercept for heart weight versus body mass), and the groups differ in body mass.
fixed: Analysis of covariance: OLS regression of heart weight on treatment status (bool) and body mass; one-sided t test on the treatment coefficient (positive, p < 0.05).
estimand: Fixed: difference in heart weight between treated and untreated animals at equal body mass (adjusted treatment effect). Faulty: difference between the groups in the mean of heart weight divided by body mass, which also moves with the groups' body-mass difference whenever the intercept is not zero.
guard_minimum: 4 animals with at least 1 animal in each group (smallest size at which the treatment coefficient and its t statistic exist: 3 parameters, 1 residual degree of freedom); zero variance of body_mass -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: CUR13 abstract states no sizes (abstract only read). 48 animals is a realistic small-animal experiment (24 per group) and is far below the 1000 cap. Timing: OLS on 48 rows about 0.2 ms per call, generation about 0.1 ms; with S about 5 the estimate 2 x 200 x (S+1) x (t+g) is under 5 s. CUR13 abstract says nothing about how the error depends on sample size: not stated.
notes: Precedence of family: the claim's threshold is on a regression coefficient (of a bool predictor), so regression-slope precedes mean. Setting is generic physiological normalisation (CUR13 abstract: ratio 'to compute a proportion for some biological response or to derive some standardized variable'); heart weight and body mass are my illustration, not a CUR13 example. Claim names body mass because the fixed estimand conditions on it. In the claim-false world (adjusted effect <= 0 or not significant) with a non-zero intercept and treated animals lighter, the quotient is larger in the treated group.

passage: Abstract: 'In each situation, we want to control for differences in the denominator when the thing we really care about is the numerator. But there is peril lurking in a ratio: only if the relationship between numerator and denominator is a straight line through the origin will the ratio be meaningful.' Correction: regression including analysis of covariance.
faulty: Pearson correlation across participants between age and the albumin-to-creatinine quotient (albumin excretion divided by creatinine excretion); claim holds when r >= 0.15. Documented parameter: numerator-denominator relation not through the origin (albumin excretion has a positive intercept against creatinine excretion), and the denominator varies with age (creatinine excretion falls with age).
fixed: Partial correlation of albumin excretion and age given creatinine excretion (residuals of each on creatinine excretion, then Pearson r); claim holds when partial r >= 0.15.
estimand: Fixed: the correlation between albumin excretion and age at fixed creatinine excretion. Faulty: the correlation between age and the albumin-to-creatinine quotient, which also reflects how creatinine excretion changes with age.
guard_minimum: 4 participants (partial correlation with one covariate has 1 residual degree of freedom at n = 4; n = 3 gives a perfect fit); zero variance of any variable or of a residual -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: CUR13 abstract states no sizes. 800 is a realistic cohort/survey size for urinary studies and fits the cap (1000); partial correlation costs microseconds, estimate well under 10 s. Dependence of the error on n: not stated (the spurious part does not shrink with n).
notes: Setting (24-hour excretions of albumin and creatinine, age) is my illustration of CUR13's 'normalized data'; excretions rather than concentrations chosen so hydration does not itself create a shared factor. Faulty sign: if creatinine excretion falls with age and the albumin line has a positive intercept, the quotient rises with age. Claim states the quantity required by the fixed estimand (creatinine excretion).

passage: Abstract: 'we compute a ratio-a numerator divided by a denominator-to compute a proportion for some biological response or to derive some standardized variable ... regression techniques-these include analysis of covariance-are versatile.' (Europe PMC record, PMID 24022766.)
faulty: R-squared of the simple regression of systolic pressure on left ventricular mass divided by body surface area (the standardised variable as the only predictor); claim holds when R-squared >= 0.05. Documented parameter: numerator-denominator relation not through the origin (LV mass has a non-zero intercept against body surface area), outcome varies with the denominator.
fixed: Gain in R-squared when left ventricular mass is added to the regression of systolic pressure on body surface area (R2 of the 2-predictor model minus R2 of the 1-predictor model); claim holds when gain >= 0.05.
estimand: Fixed: extra variance of systolic pressure explained by left ventricular mass once body surface area is in the model. Faulty: variance of systolic pressure explained by the mass-to-surface-area quotient alone, which carries information about body surface area.
guard_minimum: 4 patients (2 predictors plus intercept: 1 residual degree of freedom; the R-squared gain is defined from n = 4); zero variance of any variable -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: CUR13 abstract states no sizes. 300 patients is a realistic clinic series; OLS on 300 rows about 0.3 ms, estimate under 10 s. Dependence on n: not stated.
notes: Here the normalised variable is the predictor (CUR13: 'standardized variable'); the outcome is the variable that varies with the denominator, so the tag is ratio-vs-denominator-proxy and not ratio-shared-denominator. Illustrative setting, not a CUR13 example.

passage: Abstract: 'In each situation, we want to control for differences in the denominator when the thing we really care about is the numerator ... If not, the ratio will misrepresent the true relationship between numerator and denominator.' Regression with the denominator (analysis of covariance) is the correction.
faulty: Slope of the simple regression of liver weight divided by body mass on kidney weight divided by body mass (both organ weights standardised to body mass); claim holds when slope >= 0.25. Documented parameter: organ weights are not in direct proportion to body mass (non-zero intercepts); body mass varies widely across mice.
fixed: Coefficient of kidney weight in the OLS regression of liver weight on kidney weight and body mass; claim holds when coefficient >= 0.25.
estimand: Fixed: change in liver weight per unit kidney weight at fixed body mass. Faulty: slope between the two mass-standardised variables, which includes the common body-mass term.
guard_minimum: 4 mice (3 parameters, 1 residual degree of freedom); zero variance of kidney_weight or collinearity making the coefficient undefined -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: CUR13 abstract states no sizes. 150 mice is a larger rodent cohort; cost under 1 ms per call, estimate under 10 s. Dependence on n: not stated.
notes: Differs from B3-07 (per-species slopes in a two-axis panel) and from B3-05/B3-06 (correlation). Threshold 0.25 is in g per g and must be reachable in plus worlds; the world author chooses the scale. Illustrative setting.

passage: Section (1): 'a biologist takes the triplet femur, tibia, humerus, and seeks the correlation between the indices femur/humerus and tibia/humerus ... there would be ... a correlation of about 0.4 to 0.5 between these indices had the bones been sorted absolutely at random.' (OCR text of Proc. R. Soc. 60:489, archive.org philtrans00847732.)
faulty: Pearson correlation across skeletons between femur_length/humerus_length and tibia_length/humerus_length; claim holds when r >= 0.3. Documented parameter: equal coefficients of variation of the three lengths give r about 0.5 (Pearson's example 0.45) when the lengths are otherwise uncorrelated.
fixed: Partial correlation of femur_length and tibia_length given humerus_length; claim holds when >= 0.3.
estimand: Fixed: correlation between femur and tibia length at fixed humerus length. Faulty: correlation between the two quotients over the same humerus length, which contains the shared humerus term.
guard_minimum: 4 skeletons (partial correlation with 1 covariate); zero variance of any variable or residual -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: PEA97 text: 'some thousand individuals' and '1000 skeletons' in illustrations; 1000 used (at the cap, size ratio about 1). Cost of the fixed criterion under 1 ms; estimate under 10 s. Dependence of the error: PEA97 gives a population formula depending on the coefficients of variation and correlations, r about 0.5 for equal coefficients of variation, not on n; as a second-order approximation (cubes of relative deviations neglected).
notes: Pearson's own example and organ setting. Claim names humerus length because the fixed estimand conditions on it.

passage: Section (1): 'it was convenient to divide the errors made by three observers in estimating a variable quantity by the actual value of the quantity. As a result there appeared a high degree of correlation between three series of absolutely independent judgments.' (OCR text, p. 490.)
faulty: Relative error of each observer on each trial: (estimate minus true value) divided by true value; mean over the three observer pairs of the Pearson correlation of relative errors across trials; claim holds when the mean >= 0.2. Documented parameter: three observers, true value varies from trial to trial.
fixed: For each of the three observer pairs, the partial correlation of the two observers' estimates given true_value across trials; the mean over the three pairs; claim holds when mean >= 0.2.
estimand: Fixed: mean association between observers' estimates after removing the true value (shared judgement tendencies). Faulty: mean correlation of the observers' errors expressed relative to the common true value.
guard_minimum: 4 trials (partial correlation with 1 covariate); fewer than 2 observers -> None; zero variance of any residual -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: PEA97 states 'three observers' (kept, observers = 3) and no number of trials; 200 trials is a typical psychophysics session and keeps cost under 5 ms per call (3 partial correlations); estimate under 15 s. Dependence on n: not stated (population formula).
notes: Differs from B3-05 in the data structure (two-axis estimates array, aggregation over observer pairs). Estimates are in true-value units so partial correlation given the true value equals the correlation of residual deviations.

passage: Section (1): 'It has hitherto been usual to measure the organic correlation of the organs of shrimps, prawns, crabs, &c, by the correlation of indices in which the denominator represents the total body length or total carapace length.' (OCR text, p. 490.)
faulty: For each species, the slope of the regression of claw_length/body_length on abdomen_length/body_length across individuals; mean of the per-species slopes; claim holds when the mean >= 0.15. Documented parameter: both indices share the total body length as denominator.
fixed: For each species, the OLS coefficient of abdomen_length in the regression of claw_length on abdomen_length and body_length across individuals; mean over species; claim holds when the mean >= 0.15.
estimand: Fixed: mean within-species change in claw length per unit abdomen length at fixed body length. Faulty: mean within-species slope between the two body-length-standardised variables.
guard_minimum: 4 individuals in a species (3 parameters, 1 residual degree of freedom) else that species is skipped; no usable species -> None; zero variance -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: PEA97 states no sizes for the crustacean setting. 15 species x 40 individuals = 600 values per array, within the cap; 15 small regressions per call, about 3 ms, estimate under 30 s. Dependence on n: not stated.
notes: Family is a summary (mean) of per-unit slopes, as the definition of regression-slope allows. Differs from B3-04 by the species x individuals structure.

passage: Abstract: 'Type 3, the most common type of mathematic coupling, is direct algebraic coupling between two variables, when one or more of the variables is derived and/or calculated ... The common problem in each type of mathematic coupling is that one variable either directly or indirectly contains the whole or components of the second variable.' (Europe PMC record, PMID 7212790; abstract only.)
faulty: Pearson correlation across patients between the fall (sbp_baseline_first minus sbp_week12) and sbp_baseline_first; claim holds when r >= 0.3. Documented parameter: the change contains the baseline reading it is related to; each reading has its own measurement error.
fixed: Pearson correlation between the fall (sbp_baseline_first minus sbp_week12) and sbp_baseline_second, the second reading at the same baseline visit; claim holds when r >= 0.3.
estimand: Fixed: relation of the fall to the baseline level measured by a reading that does not enter the fall. Faulty: relation of the fall to the very reading it is computed from.
guard_minimum: 3 patients (smallest size at which a Pearson correlation is defined); zero variance of the fall or of the second reading -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: ARC81 abstract states no sizes. 120 patients is a realistic trial arm; cost microseconds. Dependence on n: not stated; the size of the artefact depends on the ratio of measurement-error variance to between-patient variance (my reasoning, not from the abstract).
notes: The correction as documented in the abstract is recognition of the coupling and analysis of a relation that does not contain the coupled component; the independent second reading is my choice of the corrected analysis (the full text is not open, so the paper's own correction is not read). Claim names the second baseline reading because the estimand requires the independent measurement.

passage: Abstract: 'Type 2 coupling is the functional relationship between two calculated variables which have one or more common component variables.' (Europe PMC record, PMID 7212790; abstract only.)
faulty: Pearson correlation across patients between oxygen delivery (cardiac_output times arterial_o2_content) and oxygen uptake calculated from the same cardiac output (cardiac_output times (arterial_o2_content minus venous_o2_content)); claim holds when r >= 0.3. Documented parameter: both calculated variables contain cardiac output, which carries its own measurement error.
fixed: Pearson correlation between oxygen delivery (cardiac_output times arterial_o2_content) and o2_uptake_expired, the uptake measured by expired-gas analysis; claim holds when r >= 0.3.
estimand: Fixed: relation between oxygen delivery and an uptake measure that does not contain cardiac output. Faulty: relation between delivery and an uptake calculated from cardiac output.
guard_minimum: 3 patients (Pearson correlation); zero variance of delivery or of the uptake -> None; non-finite -> None.
sizes_note: ARC81 abstract states no sizes. 60 patients is a realistic intensive-care study. Cost microseconds. Dependence on n: not stated; artefact depends on the share of the variance of the measured common term (cardiac output).
notes: The delivery/uptake setting is my choice of an example of the abstract's Type 2 definition; citing papers in the critical-care literature (titles on oxygen delivery and consumption, e.g. PMC464119's record) cite Archie, but the setting is not read in the source itself (abstract only): see the log. The faulty criterion ignores the key o2_uptake_expired; the claim names how uptake was measured because the estimand requires the independent measurement.

passage: Abstract: 'Type 3 ... direct algebraic coupling between two variables, when one or more of the variables is derived and/or calculated ... one variable either directly or indirectly contains the whole or components of the second variable.' (Europe PMC record, PMID 7212790; abstract only.)
faulty: Label = total over all eight items >= 12; AUC of the item 1 score for that label; claim holds when AUC >= 0.65. Documented parameter: the label is calculated from a total that contains item 1.
fixed: Label = total over items 2 to 8 >= 12; AUC of the item 1 score for that label; claim holds when AUC >= 0.65.

Dependence on n: not stated; the part of the AUC from the shared item shrinks as the number of items grows (my reasoning: item 1 is 1/8 of the total).
notes: Statistic family classification by definition (AUC of a predictor of a categorical outcome). Claim states the items entering the label because the estimand requires an outcome defined without the predictor.
